svg.text: Which Mac mini runs which models (decode speeds from community benchmarks)
Decode tok/s scales with memory bandwidth: tok/s ~ bandwidth / model size in GB (Q4 quant ~ 0.6 GB per B params)
TIER 1 - Mac mini M6 (16-32 GB, 170 GB/s, from $899)
8B-14B models at Q4. Fast chat, RAG, agents-lite, embeddings, Whisper-class audio.
8B Q4 ~ 25-35 tok/s (estimate: ~60% of M4 Pro speeds at 170 vs 273 GB/s). Prompt processing up to 4.8x faster than M4 mini (LM Studio).
First Mac mini with Neural Accelerators in every GPU core + dual 16-core Neural Engine.
TIER 2 - Mac mini M4 Pro 48 GB (273 GB/s, ~$1,999) - THE SWEET SPOT
Qwen 3.6-35B-A3B MoE Q4 (19-20 GB): 30-50 tok/s - TTFT 210-380 ms. Llama 3.1 8B Q4: 55-65 tok/s llama.cpp, 70-80 MLX.
Qwen3-14B Q4: 20-28 tok/s. Qwen3-32B dense: 12-17 tok/s. Llama 70B Q4: ~14 tok/s. Thunderbolt 5 for clustering.
MoE models decode like small models (3B active of 35B) while storing big-model knowledge.
~40 W under AI load, ~5 W idle - roughly $25/year of electricity running around the clock.
TIER 3 - Mac mini M5 Pro (up to 64 GB, from $1,699)
307 GB/s - above M4 Pro's 273 - with 64 GB headroom: 70B Q4/Q5 comfortably, long-context 35B MoE serving.
Fits Qwen 3.6-35B-A3B Q6 (27-29 GB) or Qwen 3.6-27B dense Q6 (~22-30 GB) with room for 262K context KV cache.
Announced Aug 25, 2026; on sale Sep 22, 2026. Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, optional 10 GbE.
TIER 4 - Cluster of 4-8 Mac minis via EXO (Thunderbolt 5 RDMA)
Pool 192-384 GB of unified memory. Published 8x M4 Pro cluster runs DeepSeek V3 671B at 5.37 tok/s.
Also feasible: Qwen3-235B-A22B 4-bit (~120 GB, 2+ nodes), Llama 4 Maverick 400B (~40B active).
Only MoE models cluster well - active experts ship between nodes, weights stay put.
Sources: Apple newsroom (Aug 2026), InsiderLLM, SpecPicks, RunAIHome, compute-market.com, LocalScore - speeds vary with runtime, quant and context.
